- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:521-525 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_escalate_fixup` filters lines before stripping trailing CR characters, so a CR-only line can be selected as the last non-blank line and prevent recognition of an existing escalation marker.
  WHY: For CRLF-formatted comment bodies ending with a blank CRLF line, the selected line becomes empty after CR stripping instead of matching the marker, causing repeated escalation.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:504 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_try_regrant` posts the regrant marker before all regrant operations have succeeded, so a later operation failure leaves a marker that prevents retrying.
  WHY: A subsequent run interprets the marker as proof that regrant succeeded, even if label removal or the resume command failed.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:494-495 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The regrant marker is posted before the resume actions, so a later operation failure leaves a marker that prevents retrying the automatic resume.
  WHY: The operation runner stops after a failure at 170-174, and on the next judge run the rejection is classified as already re-granted even if the current guard still grants the paths.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  WHY: This could cause the judge to re-escalate.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: line 504 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_try_regrant` posts the regrant marker comment as part of a batch of operations, and if subsequent operations (e.g., label removal) fail, future runs skip retrying the operation due to the marker's presence.
  WHY: The unblock judge relies on the presence of the regrant marker to deduce that the re-grant operation was already successful (`already_regranted`). If the comment posting succeeds but label removal or the resume command fails, the issue remains blocked, but its history erroneously suggests the re-grant was already successful, permanently preventing any further retry attempts and requiring manual intervention.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: lines 511 (unblock_fixup_origin, updated this run) vs. lines 521-525 (unblock_escalate_fixup, NOT updated) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_fixup_origin` strips CR per line before the non-blank filter, but `unblock_escalate_fixup` filters first and strips CR only on the chosen element.
  WHY: When a CRLF-formatted comment carrying the escalation marker ends with `\r\n\r\n`, `unblock_escalate_fixup` can select `"\r"` as the last non-blank element, strip it to `""`, and fail to recognize the existing marker, causing repeated escalation.
- Requirement: "The new test exercises the CRLF (CR-only line) edge case independently so a regression that drops only the CR-strip step (not the `first`/`last` change) is caught on its own."
  Expected change site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py around line 2295 (the new `test_judge_escalates_a_blocked_project_fixup_with_a_leading_blank_line` and its sibling `test_judge_escalates_a_fixup_only_once`).
  Evidence of absence: The new test uses body `"\n" + FIXUP_BODY` (LF leading blank) and the dedup test uses body `"listed\n\n<!-- ... -->"` (LF trailing blank). Neither constructs a CRLF body (e.g. `"\r" + FIXUP_BODY` or `"listed\r\n\r\n<!-- ... -->"`) that exercises the pre-CR-strip path in isolation. The new `unblock_fixup_origin` change is partially pinned, but `unblock_escalate_fixup` — which is the function the LAST RUN DIFF left asymmetric — has no regression test for the CR-only edge case at all. A reviewer cannot tell from the tests that the CRLF asymmetry under CORRECTNESS & LOGIC above is real.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: 494-495; the regrant operations are executed by unblock_run_ops, which stops subsequent operations after a failure (170-174) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The regrant marker is posted before the resume actions. If adding the awaiting-approval label or removing ai:scope-blocked fails, the runner skips the remaining actions, but the marker remains.
  WHY: On the next judge run, that rejection is classified as already re-granted, so the automatic resume is not retried even if the current guard still grants the paths. The issue instead returns to model adjudication, which can recreate the operator-step or fix-up this change is intended to avoid.
